article.title: Hate State – Discrimination on Colorado’s Ballot w/Ann Marie Awad
article.author: Cayden Mak
article.content: In 1992, the state of Colorado let voters decide to whether to discriminate against LGBTQ individuals by proposing Amendment 2, a law that would prohibit the state from enforcing anti-discrimination protections on the basis of sexual orientation. Voters passed it and earned Colorado the moniker “hate state” in certain circles. More than 30 years later, hate is back on the ballot in Colorado. Source
